experiment.hypothesis: A ResNet18 with CIFAR-style stem (3x3 stride-1, no max-pool) and hierarchical channel progression (64-128-256-512) will achieve competitive validation accuracy (~0.99+) on 28x28 PathMNIST by leveraging local convolutional receptive fields that capture texture and nuclear morphology at multiple scales. The inductive bias of progressive downsampling with residual connections may be particularly effective for distinguishing confusable tissue classes (smooth muscle vs stroma, background vs debris) through learned hierarchical feature maps, potentially matching or exceeding the compact_transformer's 0.9929 without the overhead of self-attention.

decision.rationale: The best result so far is t0004 (compact_transformer, hidden=256, depth=6) with best val_acc ~0.9929 at epoch 27. The research explicitly identifies resnet18 as the 'strongest CNN baseline' and the critical comparison point: 'If compact_transformer does not clearly exceed resnet18 on validation, the transformer inductive bias is not justified.' No CNN has been tested yet. ResNet18's CIFAR-style 3x3 stride-1 stem preserves 28x28 spatial resolution, and its hierarchical channel progression (64-128-256-512) provides a fundamentally different inductive bias (local convolutional receptive fields vs global attention) that may better capture the texture and morphological cues needed to distinguish confusable histopathology classes. I use AdamW with lr=3e-4 (higher than the transformer's 1e-4, as CNNs benefit from higher LRs with AdamW), weight_decay=1e-2 (standard for CNNs vs 1e-4 for transformers), label_smoothing=0.1, and dropout=0.3 on the FC head. 40 epochs with patience 10 gives the CNN adequate time to converge, as CNNs typically need more epochs than transformers at this scale.
